static_traits.name: Lin Kexin
static_traits.family_status: Parents are from Japan; the client lives alone in Toronto, Canada
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with friends are tense due to money anxiety; although having close friends to confide in, hard to talk about financial fears
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; without similar past financial anxiety problems; has not yet received counseling or therapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, well-organized, able to describe feelings and situations concretely; highly cooperative; emotionally tense but able to reflect and discuss goals

basic_info.main_problem: After overspending on an expensive pair of shoes, persistently fearing 'going broke and having to move back in with parents', with marked anxiety and guilt before and after shopping, affecting sleep, diet, work, and interpersonal relationships.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to reduce fear and anxiety about finances, stay independent without becoming a burden on parents; reducing impulse spending and gaining a sense of control over expenses by setting an 'affordable weekly spending cap', tracking expenses, making shopping lists, etc.

core_beliefs: I cannot trust myself to manage money properly; once I err I will lose my independence.
If I spend money unwisely, I will become a burden on my parents.

special_situations.event: After buying that expensive pair of shoes, realizes the overspending
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If one spending episode gets out of control, it may quickly lead to financial collapse and loss of independence
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Adopts a strict budget, carries only a small amount of cash, and limits shopping to avoid making mistakes again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will spend all the money and have to move back in with my parents.

special_situations.event: Before preparing to buy anything (such as a cup of coffee)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot perfectly control spending every time, I will slide toward worse consequences
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding shopping scenarios, repeatedly checking whether something is 'really needed', repressing desires
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I buy now, it will become more and more out of control and I will fall into financial difficulty.

special_situations.event: Checking bills or balance and noticing recent spending
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Negative numbers prove my financial management is terrible, meaning the future will also go wrong
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Further cuts social spending; reduces non-essential consumption
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: See, I am terrible at managing money; this will cause big problems sooner or later.

special_situations.event: Even after following the budget for a while, reviews own spending
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Doing well does not count either; the slightest relaxation leads to failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating existing progress, continuing to tighten restrictions and monitoring
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These do not count for much; I am still far from good enough.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to maintain financial and life independence, gaining recognition without becoming a burden
core_conflict.fear: Afraid of losing independence, being forced to return to my parents and being seen as a burden
defense_goal: Reducing uncertainty and anxiety through strict self-control and rational planning, avoiding another 'out-of-control' spending episode

object_relations.self_representation: A person prone to mistakes who needs high self-restraint so as not to drag others down
object_relations.object_representation: Parents who may demand dependence or judge own improper spending

object_relations.self_representation: The 'hard-to-talk-to person' among friends who withdrew due to money anxiety
object_relations.object_representation: Friends who find her anxiety hard to understand and may grow distant

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When counseling focuses on the feelings of money anxiety itself, or when invited to stop over-controlling and try more flexible strategies
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Equates relaxing control with 'losing control' and danger, believing only more plans and rules are safe
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Preferring objective, strategic, step-by-step language, listing plans and data, avoiding exploration of vulnerable emotions as much as possible, in a steady, restrained tone.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing the overspending on that shoe purchase and its consequences
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously attributing too much responsibility to herself, worrying about being judged as 'irresponsible'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using self-blaming and apologetic phrasing, downplaying her achievements and reasonable needs, in a lowered tone, emphasizing 'I should not'.

manifestations: Strongly emphasizes maintaining economic independence and the right to self-determination; worries about being forced to return to her parents because of money problems
Although having close friends, hard to share financial fears; relationships with friends tense due to anxiety
outcomes: Social withdrawal and a sense of alienation

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treating 'never being a burden on parents, must stay independent' as an absolute standard
Using strict budgets and restrictions as self-demands, hard to allow flexibility

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Highly vigilant and self-blaming even about small spending
Overly cautious in expressing needs and communicating money topics with friends

positive_force: Has stable work and functioning level (elementary school teacher)
Willing to seek help and cooperate with counseling, able to set and accept concrete goals
Willing to try strategies such as budgeting, recording expenses, and shopping lists
Physically healthy, without serious physical illness
Has some social support (has close friends)
negative_force: Negative thinking such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, mental filtering, and predicting the future maintains anxiety
High fear and guilt about 'becoming a burden'
Excessive self-monitoring and rigid rule-mindedness reduce flexibility
Avoiding money topics leads to insufficient use of interpersonal support
Sleep and diet impaired, decline in work concentration, which in turn worsens worries

target_behavior.behavior: High-intensity anxiety and repeated worry related to shopping (with avoidance and over-control)
antecedent: Thinking about spending money before a purchase (e.g., buying coffee)
Recalling the overspending incident when buying shoes
target_behavior.core_reason: One overspending incident was catastrophized and overgeneralized, triggering strong fear and guilt about losing independence and becoming a parental burden
target_behavior.function: Escaping uncertainty and guilt, seeking safety and control
target_behavior.consequence: Sleep and diet disturbance, work affected, tense relationships with friends, declining quality of life
